prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Reform UK’s Contract argues Britain has vast potential, unleashed by Brexit, but has been betrayed by both Tories and Labour: record taxes, debt, waste, and nanny-state rules have wrecked the economy; mass immigration and the small boats crisis have strained housing and services, fostered separate communities, and undermined British culture and values; “woke” ideology and transgender activism are harming children; Net Zero has driven up energy costs, hurt industry, and forced drivers off the road. The two-party system has failed; only Reform UK offers common-sense change, restoring sovereignty over borders, money, and laws.

Core pledges
- Smart immigration, not mass immigration: freeze non-essential migration.
- No more small boats: detain and deport; return boats to France if needed.
- Zero NHS waiting lists: still free at point of use, but reformed and focused on frontline care.
- Make work pay: raise the income tax threshold to £20,000.
- Affordable energy: scrap Net Zero and green levies; unlock UK oil and gas.

Key policies
- Immigration: leave the ECHR; create a Department of Immigration; offshore fast processing and secure detention; bar asylum/citizenship for arrivals from safe countries; immediate deportation of foreign criminals; ban student dependents; five-year residency/work requirement for benefits; employer immigration tax to prioritise British workers.
- Slash waste: stop paying QE interest to commercial banks; save 5% across departments without touching frontlines; cut foreign aid by 50%; scrap thousands of EU-era rules; improve HMRC collection.
- Economy (personal): lift income tax start to £20k; cut energy taxes and levies; deep stamp duty cuts; restore VAT-free tourist shopping; spare 98% of estates from IHT (0–£2m).
- Economy (business): lift corporation tax threshold to £100k; cut main rate to 20% then 15%; abolish IR35; raise VAT threshold to £150k; abolish business rates for high-street SMEs, fund with a 4% online delivery tax; slash red tape and simplify the 21,000-page tax code.
- NHS: zero basic-rate tax for NHS and care staff for 3 years; end training caps and write off fees via service; use independent capacity; 20% tax relief on private care and insurance; voucher guarantees for GP/specialist/operations wait times; cut waste and unnecessary managers; Pharmacy First; public inquiry into excess deaths and vaccine harms.
- Energy/Net Zero: scrap Net Zero and subsidies; fast-track North Sea and shale; accelerate SMRs and other secure domestic supply.
- Law and order: recruit 40,000 officers; zero-tolerance policing; tougher sentencing with mandatory life for violent repeat offenders; build 10,000 detention places; end DEI-driven two-tier policing.
- Education: patriotic curriculum; ban transgender ideology in schools; 20% tax relief on independent schooling; scrap student loan interest; restore free speech and discipline.
- Benefits: work first; two-strike job offer rule; face-to-face assessments.
- Sovereignty and defence: scrap retained EU law and the Windsor Framework; strengthen NATO role; raise defence spending to 3% within 6 years; protect troops from lawfare; dedicated veterans department.
- Housing and families: fast-track brownfield; prioritise locals in social housing; restore landlord mortgage interest relief; support marriage; protect single-sex spaces.
- Transport/utilities: scrap HS2; end ULEZ/LTNs and EV mandates; new 50:50 public/UK-pension ownership model for utilities.
- Farming/fishing: back production, not rewilding; stop EU access abuses; ban supertrawlers; rebuild fleets and processing.
- Constitutional/culture: leave ECHR; reform Lords and civil service; tighten postal voting; free-speech bill; replace Equalities Act/DEI; reform BBC and scrap licence; reject WEF/WHO overreach; anti-corruption unit.

Funding claim: up to £160bn a year from waste cuts, scrapping Net Zero costs, benefits reform, and pro-growth measures versus £141bn in programme costs. Reform UK pledges to restore a free, proud, independent Britain.
